claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure with multilevel chemical fluctuations.
The reported hierarchical state has grain sizes between 10 and 100 nm.
A PI-GNN trained on multiscale microstructural descriptors can predict Young's modulus for HfNbTiVAl10 within 5% of experiment.
The PI-GNN can predict yield strength for HfNbTiVAl10 within 5% of experiment.
The PI-GNN can predict fracture toughness for HfNbTiVAl10 within 5% of experiment.
The proposed method will reduce computational time by more than 50-fold relative to a CALPHAD, DFT, and FEA workflow.
Graphs of phase domains, composition gradients, interphase boundaries, and dislocation networks adequately represent the mechanically relevant hierarchical microstructure.
Embedding elasticity and energy-based fracture criteria in message-passing layers enables learning of the coupling between local composition or structure and bulk mechanical response.
The PI-GNN can model that coupling without full-scale DFT calculations or finite-element meshing.
Young's modulus can be predicted to within 2 GPa.
Yield strength can be predicted to within 25 MPa.
Fracture toughness can be predicted to within 0.5 MPa·m^0.5.
Inference will take less than 10 minutes per specimen on one GPU.
The current CALPHAD, first-principles, and FEA pipeline has approximately 10% prediction error.
The current CALPHAD, first-principles, and FEA pipeline requires more than 1000 GPU-hours per alloy-design iteration.
Predictions become unreliable when composition differs from nominal HfNbTiVAl10 by more than 2 at%.
Predictions become unreliable when grain sizes exceed 100 nm.
Predictions become unreliable for processing routes outside the training domain, including additive manufacturing.
GNN methods have been successfully applied to other high-entropy alloys.
The proposed approach has not been validated for fracture toughness in refractory alloy systems.
